Because this gate closes on self-attestation with no independent reviewer, its checks are stated explicitly below and are held to HIGHER scrutiny than a crew-reviewed gate. This gate exists to satisfy the project planning invariant 'diagnose before fixing when the premise is uncertain': issue #690 inherits #664-T2's diagnosis and its issue text is known-stale. g2-implement.title: g2 Per-class allocation law + width-shape tests: implement
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. TASK: in src/physics/utilization/class_utilization_observable.py add ONE public pure function `allocate_sigma_to_classes(sigma_session: float, time_share_by_class: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` (export it in __all__, beside the existing onesided_sigma_from_grip / grip_band / grip_scale_from_store — this module already exposes exactly this kind of pure numeric helper, so the seam is the one already there, not a new one). It returns `sigma_session * time_share_by_class`, validating that the weights are finite, non-negative, and sum to 1.0 within the module's existing tolerance idiom, with a failure message naming field, expectation, and actual value. Then make compute_class_utilization_observable its single production caller: obtain the real lap's per-class shares by calling the EXISTING public class_ledger.class_time_ledger(segment_map, distance_m, v_real) — do NOT modify class_ledger.py or extend ClassDeficits (see the recorded untaken road: that would edit the frozen anti-circular core for a micro-optimisation). Replace the dataclass field g_sigma_onesided: float with TWO fields: g_sigma_onesided_by_class: np.ndarray (shape (2+k), W-column order) and g_sigma_session_s: float. RETIRE the old field name rather than re-pointing it, so any missed caller fails loudly with AttributeError instead of silently reading a scalar where an array is meant. Each band takes its OWN class's sigma. Update the module docstring's 'Binding pre-ruling' section, which currently asserts a single shared scale. TESTS in tests/unit/physics/test_class_utilization_observable.py — the width-shape unit test the issue's acceptance names, asserting on sigma_plus and NEVER on differences of upper_bound(): (T1) PARTITION IDENTITY sum_c sigma_plus_c == sigma_session (L2 invariant); (T2) MONOTONICITY a larger time share gets a strictly wider band; (T3) BOUND sigma_plus_c <= sigma_session for every class, equality only for a degenerate single-class lap; (T4) DEGENERATE sigma_session == 0 gives all-zero widths — this preserves today's empty-store behaviour exactly; (T5) DEGENERATE a zero-time-share class gets exactly zero width on its structurally-zero deficit; (T6) STRICT NARROWING every per-class width is <= the whole-lap width it replaces on the same inputs; (T7) the malformed-weights validation raises with a message naming field/expectation/actual.

g4-implement.title: g4 Documented rationale into the decision graph: implement
g4-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. DOC-ONLY GATE — the invariant chain below is PRE-AUTHORED as explicit postconditions so the crew verifies a frozen chain rather than inventing grep-shaped proxies for 'the document says what it should'. TASK: append a new Extension section to docs/architecture/decisions/c1-driver-utilization-design.md (that anchor already carries a '#628 Phase 3b' Extension, so follow its established shape: Extension heading with date and issue, Current Structural Consequence addendum, Review Trigger addendum). The section records the per-class allocation law as a graded decision. It MUST contain, and a reviewer checks each one by reading: (1) the law itself, sigma_plus_c = s_c * sigma_session with s_c the class time share; (2) the coherence identity sum_c sigma_plus_c = sigma_session, stated as holding on the SCALE PARAMETER of the underlying un-folded Student-t, not on folded expectations; (3) WHY linear and not quadrature — grip is a session-level common-mode effect with a session PK, so per-part uncertainties add linearly under perfect correlation, mirroring the point-side identity sum_c time_deficit_c = lap_time_deficit_s; (4) the three rejected alternatives with their reasons — sqrt-share (the independent-errors composition, wrong correlation model, over-widens small classes), deficit-proportional (makes the width depend on the quantity it bounds, a #628-flavoured circularity), and grip-sensitivity weighting (physically better but mints a per-class weighting grip does not carry, i.e. re-fitting grip, out of scope); (5) the stated, UNMEASURED assumption that grip perturbs a lap uniformly per unit time; (6) the honest scope limit — #690 alone does NOT make the #712/#670 held-out diagnostic informative; #721 removes the pace level and the ~1e9 magnitude, #690 removes the residual per-class over-width; (7) an @grade tag welded to each recorded decision line. Do NOT edit docs/architecture/packets/physics.md — the packet's two g_sigma_onesided lines are Cartographer's to reconcile at the spine's reconcile step, and a mid-run map edit violates the architecture bookend.

triage_candidates.summary: Grip-sensitivity weighting instead of a flat time share: a straight is power-limited and barely grip-limited, so allocating grip uncertainty to it by time share over-weights it. A physically-weighted allocation would be better but mints a per-class grip weighting the grip fit does not carry (i.e. re-fitting grip), which #690 excludes.

The persisted driver_class_observables rows written before this change carry whole-lap sigma semantics and are a stale vintage. Regenerating them is a season-scale batch run, out of scope here and Admiral-owned. Needs an owner and a trigger.

Settle decision:690-per-class-sigma-allocation-law from guess to settled/measured by recomputing the #670 held-out coverage and log-score under linear vs sqrt-share weighting once #721 and #690 have both landed.

Issue #690's own text is stale on two counts (its hypot(mu,sigma) premise and its 'low while the grip store is empty' priority framing). The issue body should be corrected so a future reader does not re-plan from it.
